name: post-norm-placement-representable-not-executable
written_before: any code. Measured over all 117 cached plans on the wave-10 (semantics 9) binary.
baseline: wave 10 (semantics 9): GREEN 38 / AMBER 7 / RED 64 / BUG 0 / silent drops 0 / blockers 1076 / K3 7 clusters
this_is_a_revelation_wave: It is forecast to clear NO row and to leave GREEN unchanged. What it changes is what the report can SEE: seven components whose execution surface refuses to build today will build one, and the probes that currently answer nothing will answer. A wave like this is scored on whether the newly reachable findings are the ones named here — not on GREEN.

the_correction_that_found_it.what_was_claimed: The wave-10 rerank said `architecture_identity` was the causal gate: an unmatched `model_type` means no component builds, so a registry entry would retire the dependent probes for free. 51 of 64 RED rows carry that blocker.
the_correction_that_found_it.what_checking_showed: False. `phi3` and `glm4_moe` match no registered family and their components build anyway — they fall through to `GenericArch`, which is the fail-open door itself. Identity and surface are independent, and phi-4 is NOT a witness for the mechanism it was picked to prove: its surface already exists, so registering `phi3` would clear one of its two blockers and leave `original_max_position_embeddings` (declared 16384 beside `rope_scaling: null`, so no scaling block exists to hold it).
the_correction_that_found_it.what_the_real_gate_is: 25 rows say in their own finding that the surface did not build, and 23 of those are norm placement, in three shapes: 12 rows with no per-layer norm operands at all (LFM2, Nemotron-H, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; 13-36 blockers each), 7 rows that are post-norm only (OLMo-2, OLMo-3, EXAONE-4; 4-9 blockers each), and 4 rows with a lone pre-attention norm (Cohere2-MoE, Jamba2, Falcon-H1).

the_fix: `NormPlacement` knows two transformer shapes — PreOnly (two norms) and PrePost (four) — plus PreMixer. Seven rows declare a third. Judged from the references and not from the name: `Olmo2DecoderLayer.forward`, `Olmo3DecoderLayer.forward` and `Exaone4DecoderLayer.forward` are line-for-line identical — `residual = h; h = attn(h); h = post_attention_layernorm(h); h = residual + h`, and the same for the MLP. The sublayer reads the RAW residual and the norm applies to the sublayer's OUTPUT before the add. This is NOT classic post-LN (`norm(x + attn(x))`, norm after the add); the difference is which tensor the norm sees, and reading one as the other produces fluent wrong output rather than a failure. Added as `NormPlacement::PostOnly`, recognised from the operand evidence `(pre_attn false, post_attn true, pre_ffn false, post_ffn true)`, which no other judged stack produces.
representable_not_executable: The op plan REFUSES to lower it, the way `MoeRouterKind::Sigmoid` and `PositionPolicy::Relative` already refuse. That is deliberate and it is the whole shape of this wave: `LayerPlan.pre_attention_norm` is a required `NormOp` with 27 consumers across the CPU and Metal forward paths, and a post-norm stack has no such operand. Making those rows EXECUTABLE means changing where the executors apply the norm, which is a separate wave with its own parity gate. Recognising a shape must not imply implementing it.

keeps: the post-norm non-execution refusal (replacing the incomplete-surface blocker)

answers_but_still_refuses: Two keys will start ANSWERING and must still BLOCK, and predicting them apart from the ones that clear is the point of the exercise. `sliding_window_pattern` is "LLLG" on both EXAONE rows and its rule has no schema field to carry a period string (`probe_unrepresented` always refuses). `num_nextn_predict_layers` is 1 on EXAONE-4.5 and its rule represents only MTP's ABSENCE (`probe_absent_when_zero`), so a positive count mismatches. A wave that cleared either would mean the schema had quietly grown a claim it cannot honour.

revelation_table.newly_exposed_blockers_not_previously_re: 0 expected — every finding on these rows already exists; what changes is its category, from `unrepresented (no component answered)` to either representable or a stated refusal. If any row gains a SUBJECT it did not have, that is a genuine revelation and must be named and explained, not absorbed.

falsifiers: any row going GREEN — nothing here makes a post-norm stack executable

any row going AMBER — the refusal is an incomplete-execution-surface fact, not an identified-but-unimplemented COMPONENT; an AMBER here would also be dishonest while `architecture_identity` still blocks the same row
any row outside the seven changing at all
a row gaining a blocker subject it did not previously have
the four `pre_attn`-only rows or the twelve no-norm-operand rows moving — they are different shapes and this variant must not absorb them
known_limitation_not_fixed_here: Carriage is judged against the SURFACE, not against a successfully built op plan. So `rms_norm_eps` will report `carried to lowered at ExecutionSurface.norm.pre.eps -> NormOp.eps` on these seven rows even though the op plan refuses to build any NormOp for them, and even though a post-only stack has no pre-norm site. That is a pre-existing property of the instrument rather than something this wave introduces, and it is the same claim-congruence gap in a milder form than wave 10's. Recorded here so the next wave that touches these rows does not read the cleared blocker as proof the eps reached an operator.
controls_required: the new evidence arm must fail before the variant exists, with the corpus's own message (`norm operand set is neither two-norm nor four-norm (pre_attn false, post_attn true, pre_ffn false, post_ffn true)`)
a two-norm and a four-norm fixture must resolve exactly as before — the new arm must be unreachable from their operand sets
the op plan must REFUSE a PostOnly component explicitly rather than lower it as PreOnly or PrePost

result.answers_but_still_refuses_held: `sliding_window_pattern` (both EXAONE rows) and `num_nextn_predict_layers` (EXAONE-4.5) started answering and did NOT clear, exactly as predicted. Distinguishing them from the sixteen that did clear was the sharpest arm of the forecast.
result.verdict: EXACT on the semantic change — every per-row prediction hit, blockers 1076 -> 1058 as forecast, no row cleared, no row outside the seven moved. The aggregate AMBER/RED columns differ from the forecast for a separate reason, declared below.

the_forecast_caught_a_fail_open_again.first_score: 1051, not the forecast 1058. The seven rows each lost their `target.execution_surface` blocker with NOTHING replacing it: OLMo-2 fell to a single blocker, its unresolved identity.
the_forecast_caught_a_fail_open_again.what_that_meant: The op plan's refusal was real — `plan_component_ops` returned no plan and an `UnimplementedSemantic` defect — but the PLAN REPORT never consulted it, so no finding said so. The row read as one registry entry away from `text closure: every declaration has a home` while VINDEX3 could not build a single op for it. That is the looks-supported failure in its purest form, and it would have fired in the very next wave: registering `olmo2` would have turned a model this build cannot execute GREEN.
the_forecast_caught_a_fail_open_again.the_fix: `NormPlacement::unimplemented_reason()` is now the ONE authority. The op plan refuses on it and the plan report reads the same function to emit an `unsupported_component` finding on a complete-but-unlowerable surface. Two lists of what cannot be lowered would have drifted into exactly the state above, so there is one.
the_forecast_caught_a_fail_open_again.why_it_was_caught: Only because the forecast said 1058 and named what should replace the cleared blocker. A wave scored on 'blockers went down' would have booked this as a better result than predicted.

instrument_change_declared_separately.what: `arch_sweep.py` now refuses to report AMBER for a checkpoint whose `model_type` matches no registered family.
instrument_change_declared_separately.why: AMBER's own definition is 'component identified, no implementation'. Awarding it to a row whose identity is unresolved credits an identification that has not happened — the same class of error as the one above, in the instrument rather than in the compiler. It surfaced because this wave was about to emit an unsupported-component finding on seven rows with unresolved identities.
instrument_change_declared_separately.effect: 4 rows move AMBER -> RED: tencent/Hy4-preview (`hy_v4`), zai-org/GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 (`glm_moe_dsa`), zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next_text`). All four were being called identified while matching nothing. The 3 rows that remain AMBER (DeepSeek-V3.2, V4-Flash, V4-Pro) have resolved identities and a genuinely unimplemented component.
instrument_change_declared_separately.consequence_for_the_ledger: The AMBER and RED columns are NOT comparable across wave 10 -> 11. GREEN, BUG, silent drops and the blocker count are.

result.controls: The pre-fix control is the corpus itself: all seven rows reported `norm operand set is neither two-norm nor four-norm (pre_attn false, post_attn true, pre_ffn false, post_ffn true)` on the wave-10 binary, which is the exact estate the new arm reads. Beside it, `placement_evidence_reads_the_post_norm_estate` pins the discriminator (a two-norm Llama stack carrying the same `post_attention_layernorm` spelling must still read PreOnly, and a lone wrap norm must still refuse), and `a_post_norm_stack_is_refused_as_unimplemented_not_lowered_as_two_norm` pins the refusal with its own negative control — the same fixture with its pre-norms intact still lowers as four-norm.
result.what_this_wave_did_not_do: It did not make a post-norm stack executable. `LayerPlan.pre_attention_norm` is a required `NormOp` with 27 consumers across the CPU and Metal forward paths, and moving the norm to the sublayer output is a separate wave with its own parity gate. Recognising a shape is not implementing it, and the closure vocabulary now states that difference in its own defect (`UnimplementedSemantic`, the opposite of `UnjudgedSemantic`: there the value is unknown, here the operator is missing).
